notes: Los Altos is predominantly single-family residential. The R3 multifamily district suffix indicates the minimum lot area per dwelling unit in thousands of square feet (e.g., R3-4.5 = 4,500 sq ft per unit).
R1 district suffixes indicate minimum lot size in thousands of square feet (R1-10 = 10,000 sq ft min lot).
For R3 zones, max_density is calculated as 43,560 sq ft/acre divided by lot area per unit. Actual yield may be lower due to setbacks, parking, open space, and other development standards.

Several commercial zones (CD, CN, CRS, CT) allow residential in mixed-use configurations. The CD/R3 and CRS/OAD districts explicitly allow multifamily housing. Where no explicit maximum density is codified for mixed-use, density is effectively controlled by development standards (height, FAR, setbacks, parking).

In March 2022, the HCD default density for lower-income housing sites in Los Altos was updated to 30 du/ac (based on 2020 Census). Sites allowing at least 30 du/ac are presumed suitable for lower-income housing.
The General Plan Land Use Element designates single-family areas as Single-Family Small Lot, Single-Family Medium Lot (up to 4 du/net acre), and Single-Family Large Lot.
Los Altos adopted Housing Element rezoning in 2022-2023 to allow higher densities in commercial/mixed-use zones to meet RHNA of 1,958 units.

R1-10.description: Single-Family Residential District (10,000 sq ft min lot, Ch. 14.06). Standard single-family detached homes. Most common residential zone in Los Altos.

R1-H.description: Single-Family Hillside Residential District (10,000 sq ft min lot with hillside overlay, Ch. 14.08). Single-family homes on hillside lots with additional slope-sensitive development standards.

R1-20.description: Single-Family Residential District (20,000 sq ft min lot, Ch. 14.10). Single-family detached homes on larger lots.

R1-40.description: Single-Family Residential District (40,000 sq ft min lot, Ch. 14.12). Single-family detached homes on very large lots, nearly one-acre minimum.

R1-S.description: Single-Story Overlay District. Applied over R1 base zones to limit buildings to one story. Same density as underlying R1 zone.

R3-5.description: Multiple-Family Residential District (5,000 sq ft min lot area per dwelling unit, Ch. 14.18). Low-density multifamily: duplexes, small apartment buildings.

R3-4.5.description: Multiple-Family Residential District (4,500 sq ft min lot area per dwelling unit, Ch. 14.16). Low-density multifamily housing.

R3-3.description: Multiple-Family Residential District (3,000 sq ft min lot area per dwelling unit, Ch. 14.20). Medium-density multifamily housing: apartments, condominiums.

R3-1.8.description: Multiple-Family Residential District (1,800 sq ft min lot area per dwelling unit, Ch. 14.22). Higher-density multifamily housing: apartments, condominiums.

R3-1.description: Multiple-Family Residential District (1,000 sq ft min lot area per dwelling unit, Ch. 14.24). Highest-density multifamily zone in Los Altos. Apartments, condominiums.

OA.description: Office-Administrative District (Ch. 14.28). Professional and administrative offices. Standalone residential not permitted.

OA-1.description: Office-Administrative District 1 (Ch. 14.28). Professional offices with specific site standards. Standalone residential not permitted.

OA-4.5.description: Office-Administrative District (4,500 sq ft min lot, Ch. 14.28). Small-scale office district. Standalone residential not permitted.

CN.description: Commercial Neighborhood District (Ch. 14.34). Neighborhood-serving retail and services. Residential may be allowed in mixed-use per Housing Element rezoning. Density up to 25 du/ac where residential is permitted.

CD.description: Commercial Downtown District (Ch. 14.36). Downtown Los Altos retail, restaurants, services. Residential allowed in mixed-use configurations per Housing Element. No explicit maximum density; effectively up to 30 du/ac based on development standards and Housing Element assumptions.

CD/R3.description: Commercial Downtown/Multiple-Family District (Ch. 14.38). Mixed-use zone allowing both commercial and multifamily residential as permitted uses. No explicit maximum density cap; effectively up to 35 du/ac based on development standards.

CRS.description: Commercial Retail Sales District (Ch. 14.40). Retail commercial uses. Residential may be allowed in mixed-use per Housing Element. Density up to 25 du/ac where residential is permitted.

CRS/OAD.description: Commercial Retail Sales/Office-Administrative District (Ch. 14.42). Mixed commercial and office zone. Residential may be allowed in mixed-use per Housing Element. Density up to 25 du/ac where residential is permitted.

CT.description: Commercial Thoroughfare District (Ch. 14.44). Commercial uses along major thoroughfares (e.g., El Camino Real). Residential allowed in mixed-use per Housing Element rezoning. Highest commercial zone density, up to 40 du/ac.

PCF.description: Public and Community Facilities District (Ch. 14.46). Schools, parks, government facilities, churches. Residential not generally permitted.

PCF/R1-10.description: Public and Community Facilities/Single-Family Residential District. Dual-zoned for public facilities and single-family residential. Density same as R1-10.

PC.description: Planned Community District (Ch. 14.48). Density set by individual planned community development plan. Allows flexible mix of uses.

PUD.description: Planned Unit Development District (Ch. 14.50). Density set by individual PUD plan approval. Allows creative site planning with mixed housing types.

LCSPZ.description: Loyola Corners Specific Plan Zone (overlay). Mixed-use specific plan area. Density governed by the Loyola Corners Specific Plan, approximately up to 25 du/ac.

OUT.description: Unincorporated/Outside City Limits. Parcels outside Los Altos city jurisdiction. Zoning governed by Santa Clara County.

ROW.description: Right-of-Way. Public streets, roads, and utility easements. No residential development permitted.
